component.name: Atlas Player
component.summary: Play any video, with HDR tonemapping and magnet streaming

description.p: Atlas Player is built on mpv, so it plays what mpv plays: HEVC and AV1, 10-bit, HDR (tonemapped to your screen, or passed through), every subtitle format, with hardware decoding where your GPU has it. Around that it adds streaming a magnet link without waiting for the download, playing DVDs and Blu-rays with their menus, and ripping discs properly.
Features:

ul.li: Plays local files, folders and disc images; subtitles next to a video load by themselves
CD rip folders play their tracks in order, with the album's cover on screen
Audio plays exactly as recorded, or evened out if you switch normalization on
Streams magnet links while they download, with seeking; nothing is kept afterwards
Plays links from YouTube and about 1,800 other sites (through yt-dlp), MEGA and direct video URLs
Downloads videos from those sites at the quality you pick, or just the audio
DVDs and Blu-rays with their menus, Audio CDs track by track, SACD images
Rips CDs with secure reads, offset correction, AccurateRip, MusicBrainz tags and cover, FLAC or WAV, cue sheet and log
Rips DVDs to MKV (copied, or encoded with x264/x265, deinterlaced with BWDIF or QTGMC), to FLAC/WAV audio, or as a decrypted backup
HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision tonemapped to SDR, or passed through to an HDR display
Lossless PNG screenshots, frame-by-frame stepping, automatic deinterlacing
24 themes and a controls bar you can rearrange

description.p: Resume where you left off, one window for every file opened, errors said and logged, no torrent freezes
CD rip folders play with their cover, normalization starts at -3 dB, credits for everything Atlas Player is built on
QTGMC works on Windows and Linux, one folder/image button, whole title or a file per chapter
Atlas Player: the new name, icon and gold-on-navy theme; a step-by-step Rip Disc with DVD audio-only rips, title and track choice, FLAC/AAC and QTGMC

Describe this release
Thirteen new themes, a font for the interface, codec badges for audio, deinterlaced screenshots

Rip single tracks of an Audio CD; a DVD's resolution badge no longer reads 0p (interlaced video shows as 576i); torrents only play, their data always deleted; More leaves out Download video while the top bar offers it.
A controls bar you arrange yourself: drag any button, badge or readout (time left, clock, title, spaces, dividers) to the left, centre or right of the bar, or off it, in Settings, Appearance.
2.0.0-beta.3 with a complete Windows zip (beta.2 and beta.3 shipped without their libraries). The Linux build is unchanged.
2.0.0-beta.2 with security updates: .NET 10, FFmpeg 9.1, mpv 0.42, libass 0.17.5, libplacebo, libbluray and yt-dlp.

A beta of 2.0.0, not yet tried on Windows: the same as 2.0.0-beta.1 (a new look with eleven themes, a simpler controls bar, regrouped settings, themed messages over the video), with the Linux Flatpak built again.

A beta of 2.0.0, not yet tried on Windows. A new look: eleven themes (the default and its light version, Graphite, Deep Sea, Amber, Forest, Call of Duty, GTA 6, Red Dead Redemption 2, 80s Synthwave, Halloween), switched live; a simpler controls bar with a More menu; the welcome screen lists every way to open something; settings regrouped into pages, each setting named and explained in a sentence. Playback, streaming and ripping are unchanged.

MEGA desktop app links read six chunks at once (no more slow buffering); DVD rips of chosen chapters, x264 deinterlaced with BWDIF; subtitle styling; choose the controls bar's buttons; Previous / Next for folders; settings carried to a new install in one file; Settings options in their categories; the pointer back on any move; the Flatpak checked on five distributions, with fallbacks for graphics drivers it can't reach.

Drag and drop on Linux and over the video on Windows; the fullscreen pointer hides on Windows; links start by themselves after 5 s of buffer; DVD rips to H.264 or H.265 MKVs that look the same as the disc in less space; the Rip Disc window fits the screen.
Crop to 16:9 right after Resize to 4:3 crops by the right shape; the Linux build attached

CD and DVD ripping (AccurateRip, MusicBrainz, FLAC; DVD to MKV or VIDEO_TS), DSD and SACDs at 192 kHz, CD and SACD badges in the controls bar, a channels badge that follows the downmix switch, the pointer hidden in fullscreen
Stop button, torrent playlists, Resize 4:3 / Crop 16:9, streaming quality in the video menu, DVD / Blu-ray / CD / SACD images, DSD files, fixes for Space, double-click and overlapping messages
Deinterlacing only for interlaced videos, smoother playback on laptops, Developer tab and logs

Simpler Open menus with Open Link and Download Video as their own buttons; downloads list their qualities as soon as a link is pasted, and can save the audio only. DVDs and Blu-rays deinterlace with BWDIF like files do. Audio CDs and CD rips with a cue sheet play, with tracks as chapters. Hardware acceleration is decided for each video, mobius is the default tonemapping curve, and DVDs no longer lag on Windows when they first load.
DVDs and Blu-rays with their menus (Open disc, Disc menu button); downloads keep their metadata and never overwrite
Downloader with quality choice, streaming quality, Open link button, volume normalization, mono downmix, 60 Hz playback timing, Balanced rendering by default
Titles and chapters menu; menus show only the options the playing video can use; HEVC-only hardware decoding; double-click fullscreen on Windows
Fixes an error when closing the window on Windows, and support for older system libmpv on Linux
Fullscreen controls bar now really sits on the bottom edge on Linux/KDE
In fullscreen the controls bar sits on the bottom edge of the screen again, with no strip of video below it
Open folders, DVDs and Blu-rays, download YouTube videos, automatic HDR
Smooth 4K on weaker GPUs: Auto rendering uses a lighter profile for 4K
Fixes and additions from the first round of testing.

ul.li: Controls come back when you move the mouse, including in fullscreen
BWDIF or Bob deinterlacing, logarithmic volume, subtitle font size shown
Faster magnet streaming for 4K HDR, with a bigger buffer before playback starts
YouTube and other sites, MEGA file links and direct video URLs
Optional AV-receiver passthrough; the original audio plays by default

description.p: First release.

ul.li: HDR to SDR tonemapping with scene-adaptive brightness, and HDR passthrough
Magnet link streaming that downloads only the file being watched
Optional 5.1/7.1 stereo downmix, with volume never normalised
Uncompressed PNG screenshots, frame stepping and automatic deinterlacing
